question: In an LLM agent, what is a tool?
options: An external function or API the model can request to call, such as a calculator or web search
A prompt template stored on disk
A hardware accelerator used to run the model
A library used to train the model
explanation: Tools let an agent act beyond text generation by having the application execute calls and return results.

question: What does linear regression model?
options: A tree of yes or no decisions over the features
A linear relationship between input features and a continuous target value
The probability that a point belongs to each cluster
A sequence of words generated one at a time
explanation: Linear regression fits a weighted sum of features plus an intercept, usually by minimizing squared error.

question: What is sentiment analysis?
options: Translating text from one language to another
Counting how many words a document contains
Determining whether text expresses a positive, negative or neutral opinion
Correcting spelling mistakes in text
explanation: Sentiment analysis classifies the emotional tone or opinion expressed in text, such as product reviews.

question: What is underfitting?
options: A model that memorizes noise in the training data
A model trained for too many epochs
A model too simple to capture the underlying pattern, so it performs poorly even on training data
A model whose test set is larger than its training set
explanation: An underfit model has high bias: it misses real structure, so both training and test error stay high.

subject: ai
question: What is clustering?
options: Predicting a numeric value from labeled examples
Removing duplicate rows from a dataset
Sorting data points by a single feature
Grouping similar data points together without using labels
explanation: Clustering is an unsupervised task that discovers groups of similar points on its own.

subject: ai
question: In supervised learning, what is a label?
options: The known target value the model learns to predict
A tag marking a row as training or test data
A name given to each column of the dataset
The identifier of the trained model version
explanation: Labels are the ground-truth outputs paired with inputs, such as spam or not spam for an email.

subject: ai
question: What does a loss function measure during training?
options: How many parameters the model has
How far the model's predictions are from the target values
How long each training step takes
How much memory the model uses
explanation: Training minimizes the loss, so it defines what counts as a good prediction.

question: Which metric is commonly used to evaluate a regression model?
options: F1 score
Precision
Recall
Mean squared error
explanation: Mean squared error averages squared differences between predicted and actual values; the others are classification metrics.

subject: ai
question: Why is data privacy a concern when training AI models on personal data?
options: Personal data cannot be stored in digital form
Personal data makes models train more slowly
Models can memorize and later reveal personal information from their training data
Models trained on personal data cannot be deployed
explanation: Sensitive details in training data can leak through model outputs, so data handling and consent matter.

question: In binary classification, what is a false positive?
options: Predicting the negative class when the actual class is positive
Correctly predicting the negative class
Correctly predicting the positive class
Predicting the positive class when the actual class is negative
explanation: A false positive is a false alarm, such as flagging a legitimate email as spam.
